name: South Sudan

facts.religion: Christian about 60%, traditional faiths, Muslim minority

system_note: A transitional government under the 2018 peace deal.
snapshot: The world's youngest country is sliding back toward civil war, with First Vice President Riek Machar on trial and elections set for December 2026 widely doubted.
culture: South Sudan has more than 60 ethnic groups, the largest being the Dinka and Nuer, whose cattle-herding cultures place cows at the centre of wealth, marriage and poetry. Young men compose songs for their favourite oxen. Juba Arabic is the street language, English the official one.
society: South Sudan split from Sudan in 2011, and a civil war between forces loyal to Kiir and Machar killed some 400,000 people from 2013 to 2018. Oil is almost the only export, and it flows through a pipeline across war-torn Sudan. Most of the population needs humanitarian aid, and floods and refugees from Sudan add to the strain.
situation: The world's youngest country has never held a national election. South Sudan won independence in 2011 amid huge hope, and within two and a half years its president, Salva Kiir, a Dinka, and his deputy, Riek Machar, a Nuer, had led their communities into a civil war that killed some 400,000 people. A 2018 peace deal put them back in government together. In 2026, Machar spent the year on trial for treason, murder and terrorism, under house arrest, while the government insisted the first elections would finally happen in December (AP via Yahoo).

The charges stem from a March 2025 clash in Upper Nile that the government blamed on Machar's allies. His trial, with seven co-defendants, dragged past its 68th session, and the African Union called for his release to allow a ceasefire and dialogue (Radio Tamazuj). UN experts warned that the peace deal was eroding, that both sides' forces faced off across much of the country, and that an under-supplied army was relying on "relatively indiscriminate" air strikes, with Ugandan troops backing Kiir. The information minister vowed elections in December with "no further extension" (Arab News). Analysts say the trial's real purpose is to keep Machar out of any vote. Meanwhile, war in neighbouring Sudan has cut oil exports and sent refugees south, in a country where most people already depend on aid.
power: A transitional government under the 2018 peace agreement, sharing posts among Kiir's SPLM, Machar's SPLM-IO and other parties, with a president, five vice presidents and an expanded appointed parliament. In practice Kiir rules by decree, frequently firing officials without consultation.
holders: President Salva Kiir, in office since independence in 2011.

update.html: President Salva Kiir said on 26 October that general elections, never held since independence, will go ahead 'by all means' on 22 December, although voter registration only begins in November and funding is unclear; the transitional institutions of the 2018 peace deal were dissolved in September. First Vice President Riek Machar remains on trial over the March 2025 Nasir attack, and the acting leader of his SPLM/A-IO faction, Oyet Nathaniel Pierino, vowed on 2 November to keep fighting. On 19 October drone strikes on the Amiet market in Abyei killed at least 30 people by the UN's count and 153 or more according to local officials; Juba blamed the Sudanese army.
